newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-HAVELANGE TO DISCUSS WORLD CUP FENCES WITH CHIRAC.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HAVELANGE TO DISCUSS WORLD CUP FENCES WITH CHIRAC.

text.p: FIFA president Joao Havelange is expected to discuss the removal of perimeter fencing from 1998 World Cup venues with French president Jacques Chirac when the two meet in Paris next month.
A FIFA official said on Monday the issue could be discussed at a meeting between the two men on March 12.
FIFA, soccer's world governing body, want fences removed but French Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre said last week they would remain in place for the World Cup finals in France.
Nine of 10 grounds being prepared for the finals already have fencing. Fencing will also be erected at the new Stade de France being built in Paris.
"Our opinion about fences hasn't changed," FIFA spokesman Keith Cooper said on Monday.
"Certainly one has to acknowledge the authority of the country but our president will meet with Chirac and probably it will be part of the discussion.
"Until we receive formal notification from the French federation we will continue to study and discuss the situation."

FIFA has campaigned to abolish perimeter fencing in the aftermath of several stadium tragedies, including one in Sheffield, England, in 1989 at the Hillsborough ground where 96 people were crushed to death in an over-crowded, fenced-in section of terracing during an F.A. Cup semifinal between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest.
FIFA general secretary Sepp Blatter has been particularly outspoken, describing fences as cages which should be used only for animals and criminals.

The call for the removal of fencing was renewed recently when more than 80 people were killed in an incident chillingly similar to the one at Hillsborough before the start of a World Cup qualifying match in Guatemala last October.
Nine people died following a stampede at a World Cup qualifier between Zambia and Sudan in Lusaka in June.
